**The meaning of the hadith**
In this hadith the Prophet ﷺ tells of two great and noble blessings in which many people lose out: they do not know their worth and do not benefit from them in their worldly life or their life in the Hereafter. They are: health and strength of body and soul, and free time, which is a person being free from the demands of earning a living and the worries of life, with safety and peace of mind. These are two great blessings, and many people do not value them as they deserve.

This hadith indicates that a person is only free for obedience if he is provided for and healthy in body; for he may be free of need but not healthy, or healthy but not free of need, and so not free for knowledge and good deeds because he is busy earning a living. So whoever has both — health and free time — and is lazy about acts of obedience, he is the one who loses out, the loser in his trade!

The hadith encourages making use of blessings such as health, free time and others, and benefiting from them in what pleases Allah, glorified and exalted is He.

📖 From the Hadith Encyclopedia — Dorar.net.

**Talk with your child**
1. Hani and Wisam had the very same holidays. What did each of them do with them? And what was the word Hani said every day?
2. Uncle Hasan said that losing out is "like someone who sells something precious for a cheap price." What did Hani sell, and for what price?
3. Is playing always a waste of time? (No; allowed play and rest are a child's right. The one who loses out is the one whose time all goes on things that leave nothing behind, while he neglects what benefits him. And Hani did not throw the tablet away; he gave everything its own time.)

**This week's exercise**
Write "Hani's paper" together: three things your child wants to get done this week, and under each one its time (after Asr, after Isha…), plus a set time for the tablet. Hang it somewhere easy to see, and at the end of the week look together at what got done.
